findings.source_quote: Straight or crooked, one of twain;
findings.suggested_fix: Use Swahili wording that preserves the contrast between 'straight' and 'crooked' (moral/structural orientation), not 'nyororo' which means 'soft'. Replace the second stanza line with: "Iwe zenye mwelekeo sawa au zilizoinama, moja kati ya mbili;" (keep punctuation and line break structure).
findings.translation_quote: Iwe nyororo au yenye kupinda, moja kati ya mbili;

findings.location: Third stanza, line 1 (address to the audience)
findings.source_quote: O dear souls! upon life’s pathway,
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the plural address of the original ('souls' plural). Replace with a plural vocative such as: "Ewe roho mpenzi!" is singular — change to "Ewe roho mpenzi zenu!" or better: "Ewe roho mpendwa nyinyi wote!" while preserving the HTML and line break. For example: "Ewe roho mpendwa nyinyi wote! kwenye njia ya maisha,"
findings.translation_quote: Ewe roho mpenzi! kwenye njia ya maisha,

findings.location: Third stanza, line 2–4 (imperative and address-number agreement)
findings.source_quote: Lean upon your Savior’s breast;\nThere no foe can e’er molest you,\n‘Til you reach eternal rest.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix verb forms and phrasing to match plural addressees and natural Swahili idiom. Suggested replacement that preserves original meaning and poetic form: "Jikinge juu ya kifua cha Mwokozi wenu;\nHakuna adui atakayowadhuru huko,\nMpata mapumziko ya milele." (or "mpate" depending on rhythm). Keep punctuation and line breaks as in source HTML.
findings.translation_quote: Egeukeni juu ya kifua cha Mwokozi wenu;\nHakuna adui atakayekuudhi huko,\nHadi ufikie mapumziko ya milele.
